newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH MOBILE PHONE USE NEARS LOCAL FIXED-LINE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH MOBILE PHONE USE NEARS LOCAL FIXED-LINE.

text.p: The Finnish market for mobile telephone calls grew 40 percent last year in terms of net sales, making it almost as big as the local fixed-line call market, the ministry of transport and communications said on Thursday.

"Mobile communications continue to be the fastest-growing area of telecommunications in Finland," the ministry said. with 32.2 mobile phones per 100 inhabitants, Finland has the highest mobile phone density in the world.
Mobile phone calls now account for 35 percent of the Finnish market, against 36 percent for local fixed-line calls, the ministry said in a statement.
Net sales of telephone service providers in Finland grew 12.7 percent in 1996 to a total of 12.4 billion markka, the ministry said.

State-owned Telecom Finland had the biggest share of the overall market with net sales of 6.2 billion markka. The Finnet group had net sales of 5.7 billion, Telivo Oy and other operators had sales of 164 million markka.
In an OECD price comparison, Finland was among the five countries with the world's lowest mobile phone prices, the ministry said.
Finland has the second least expensive local phone call rates in the European Union, whereas local calls are cheapest in Luxembourg, a ministry official said.
Finland is also the world leader in Internet connections, with 60 per 1,000 inhabitants, the ministry said.
